Exercise the inventory movement controls at their boundary values, verify low-stock summaries, and confirm undo reverses the latest movement.

Work through these checks in order, and record what you actually observe for each:
1. On a fresh page, note Panel A3's initial 7 units. Then Record Received 3 for Panel A3, record Shipped 1, then click Undo. — expect: Panel A3 must show 10 units, one received movement, and no shipped movement.
2. Use the initial inventory and note that Panel A3 has 7 units. Then Choose Panel A3, select Shipped, enter 7, and click Record. — expect: Panel A3 must show 0 units, Low — reorder, and one shipped movement without a quantity error.
3. Use the initial inventory and note that Washer 11mm has 60 units and a reorder point of 60; note the Items low total. Then Read the Washer 11mm row and the Items low total. — expect: Washer must show Low — reorder, and Items low must include it, totaling 2 initially.

scored.why: Findings 1 and 5 explicitly report that undoing a shipment changes Panel A3 from 6 to 5 instead of restoring it to 7, i.e. it decrements stock again.
Finding 3 explicitly reports items exactly at their reorder points (Washer 60/60 and Panel A3 5/5) as OK rather than low. Finding 8 also reports Washer 11mm at its reorder level as OK.
Findings 2 and 7 explicitly report that attempting to ship all 140 on-hand BLT-04 units is rejected with “Only 140 ... on hand,” with no shipment recorded.
